title: A power series ring over a characteristic-zero field or a Cohen ring is formally smooth for its maximal-ideal-adic topology
statement: Let $n\ge0$. (1) Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$, $C=K[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ the formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], regarded as a $\mathbf Q$-algebra through $\mathbf Q\subseteq K\subseteq C$, and $\mathfrak m_C=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\subseteq C$. Then $C$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. (2) Let $p$ be a prime, $\Lambda$ a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], $C=\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ and $\mathfrak m_C=(p,x_1,\ldots,x_n)\subseteq C$. Then $C$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Z$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs, line 9704), parts (1) and (3); part (2) (F_p -> L[[x]]) is not stated here. Its proof reduces by the universal property of power series rings to Q -> K formally smooth (Algebra, Proposition 0322) and Z -> Lambda formally smooth for the m_Lambda-adic topology (Algebra, Lemma 0329 cohen-ring-formally-smooth).
